route: Romania has no dedicated independent-means permit that I could confirm. The relevant rule is the health-insurance condition on temporary residence. In OUG 194/2002 (foreigners' regime), an extension of the temporary right of residence needs 'g) prezinta dovada asigurarii sociale de sanatate' (proof of social health insurance), and permanent residence needs 'c) fac dovada asigurarii sociale de sanatate'. So the rule points to the public CASS system, not a private policy. The cached text is an older consolidated copy hosted by the Romanian Border Police; I could not reach legislatie.just.ro to confirm the current wording or article number.
policy: CASS (contributia de asigurari sociale de sanatate) paid by a person with no taxable income who opts in through the Declaratia unica (form 212, chapter II, section 1, letter E, 'Sunt persoana fara venituri'). One flat annual sum per person: 10% of the base of 6 gross minimum wages in force on 1 January 2026 (4,050 lei), so 2,430 lei a person for the year. Each spouse files and pays separately. The option can be exercised at any point in the year and covers the year.
working: 6 x 4,050 = 24,300 lei; x 10% = 2,430 lei a person a year. Two people: 4,860 lei a year; / 12 = 405 lei a month.

income_based_charges.name: CASS for people with income (Cod fiscal; article numbers not verified in this pass)
income_based_charges.base: net annual income from independent activities, rents, investments and some other sources; ANAF guidance cached here shows thresholds of 6 and 12 gross minimum wages; exact bands not verified
income_based_charges.includes_capital_gains: unclear: not checked in this pass. A couple with investment withdrawals that count as taxable investment income could owe CASS on that income instead of the flat opt-in sum. Pass to the tax agent.

eu_citizen_difference: An EU citizen resident in Romania pays the same CASS opt-in sum, or may use EHIC or an S1 from another member state. Not checked beyond that.
spot_check: Secondary Romanian press (capital.ro, alba24.ro, economica.net, digi24.ro, bzi.ro), seen only in search summaries and not cached, all give 2,430 lei for 2026. Same figure, so they agree.
uncertainty: (1) The base is fixed to the 1 January minimum wage; the minimum wage rose in July 2026 (press reports say to 4,325 lei), so a 2027 opt-in would be 6 x 4,325 x 10% = 2,595 lei a person, about 7% higher. (2) Law 141/2025 removed free co-insurance for a non-earning spouse from 1 September 2025 (press summary, not cached), so each spouse pays. (3) Whether IGI accepts the opt-in CASS payment as 'asigurarea sociala de sanatate' proof for a new non-EU resident was not confirmed from an IGI page. (4) No private tariff found, so there is no fallback figure if the public route is refused. (5) Romanian ANAF notes differ on the payment schedule (25% at filing and 75% later, or in full by 25 May of the following year); this changes timing, not the total.
